newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot plans regular flights to Malta.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot plans regular flights to Malta.

text.p: Russian flagship international carrier Aeroflot plans to begin regular flights between Russia and Malta, a senior company official said on Tuesday.
Mikhail Sen, Aeroflot regional director for Africa, said a Moscow-Malta direct link would be introduced in the summer 1997 schedule. "It will be serviced by Tupolev-154 or Ilyushin-86 jets," he said.
Currently, Aeroflot makes stopovers in Malta on flights between Moscow and Luanda, Angola, and Casablanca, Morocco. The new flight will terminate in Malta.
Yuri Vasilenko, Aeroflot's Malta representative, said Russia and Malta were likely to sign a bilateral service agreement.
Sen said Aeroflot was opening the route in response to increasing interest in the island by Russian tourists.
Vasilenko said Aeroflot carried 15,000 passengers from Russia to Malta on Africa-bound flights last year, up from 13,500 in 1995.

A Malta embassy official in Moscow said Russians on group package tours would be able to get visas at the Malta airport from March 15, though individual travellers would still have to get visas in Moscow.
